source.title: A silent eligibility trace enables dopamine-dependent synaptic plasticity for reinforcement learning in the mouse striatum.

confidence_rationale: Independent whole-cell evidence for a synapse-specific eligibility trace in striatal D1 neurons: dopamine potentiated only synapses active ~2 s before its release. Corroborates Yagishita with a different method. Mapping again capped by synapse-versus-loop grain, and the D1-only result limits generality.
failure_signatures: The trace was demonstrated in D1-expressing neurons only; the pre-post LTD component was absent in D2 neurons, so the paper does not establish the same trace mechanism in the indirect pathway.
Dopamine released at earlier or later offsets than ~2 s produced no potentiation, i.e. the trace is narrow in time; a broad trace would be a departure from this mechanism.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Pre-post spike pairing in D1 striatal neurons leaves a silent, transient trace (a 2-4 s rise in Ca-permeable AMPA receptor rectification); dopamine uncaged ~2 s after the pairing converts it into potentiation selectively at the synapses that were active, but not at earlier or later offsets.
mapping.ree_translation: A second, independent demonstration that the dopamine third factor acts only through a synapse-specific, short-lived eligibility flag -- supporting MECH-452's requirement that WHICH channels a shared delta_t updates be decided by a local trace, and its specific warning that a temporally smeared trace would misassign credit.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Synapse-level and D1-only; REE's MECH-452 applies loop-local traces to gating channels across motor/associative/limbic loops, including channels standing in for the indirect pathway where this paper found no equivalent mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Adult mouse striatal slices, whole-cell recording in D1- and D2-identified SPNs, spike-timing protocols, timed dopamine uncaging.

confidence_components.notes: Solid slice physiology in a respected journal; smaller scope than Yagishita; mapping limited by grain and D1-only finding.
